fields.subtype: Native Zune HD device port of sm64ex (decompilation-based)
fields.source_available: Public source repository. The project's own files are MIT-licensed; Fast3D-derived renderer files have separate terms that prohibit binary redistribution unless the binary contains no assets the distributor lacks rights to share. The included OpenZDK launcher uses separate BSD-style terms, and the sm64ex submodule retains its own terms. Builds require the user's own USA Super Mario 64 ROM; the maintainer offers no built game. GitHub reports Other / NOASSERTION for the mixed repository license.

fields.status: Latest release v1.1.5 was published 2026-10-15. Its notes fix a 64-bit crash on four Super Special stages, ultrawide service-area car proportions, and controller detection; local regression tests were run on Linux i686/x86-64, and release packages are built/tested by GitHub Actions for each supported platform. The current README reports playable stages on Linux x86-64/i686, Windows x86-64 (tested under Wine), and Android ARM64/x86-64. Linux ARM64 and macOS ARM64 build and pass tests, but gameplay is not yet tested there.

fields.summary: Static recompilation of the Nintendo Switch remake into native desktop applications. Setup generates and compiles the game locally from the user’s own legally obtained, extracted v1.0.0 game files; the repository and release builds include no Nintendo game files, game code, assets, or fonts. The project’s own code is MIT-licensed, while third-party components retain separate licenses. The README says the project was made almost exclusively with AI.
